items.title: Microsoft Offers Buyouts to About 60,000 Employees
items.snippet: In a bid to lower costs tied to its historic spending on AI infrastructure, Microsoft announced that it is offering buyouts to about 60,000 eligible employees. “Today, we’re introducing a new Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) to eligible employees within participating organizations,” Microsoft executive vice president Amy Coleman wrote in an email to employees today. “This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs.” The Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) follows a July voluntary retirement program targeting 7 percent of Microsoft U.S.-based employees. In that purge, about 30 percent of the 8,750 eligible employees opted to leave the company. This offer is broader and is available to eligible employees in participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States at level 70 [vice president] and below. items.title: Is it time to retire VPNs?
items.snippet: As legacy VPN vulnerabilities and AI-driven exploits expose corporate networks, zero-trust architecture is emerging as the imperative replacement, making systems invisible and preventing broad network access. For more than two decades, VPNs have been the de facto standard and the default way to connect remote users to the corporate network. It worked when employees sat in offices and applications ran in the data center. That world is gone, but the VPN has stuck around, and the security bill is now coming due.
